Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

glory noun

also fame, renown, distinction, splendour, the pride of, an ornament to, credit

classical

Cic. de Or. 2.154: nōn tulit ūllōs haec cīvitās aut glōriā clāriōrēs aut auctōritāte graviōrēs (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Tusc. 3.3: est enim glōria solida quaedam rēs et expressa, nōn adumbrāta (Lewis & Short)

glōria, glōriae f.

noun, first declension

glory, fame, renown

Other words

  • decus, decoris n. — what adorns or does credit: an ornament, distinction, honour

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Caecin. 28: decus atque ōrnāmentum jūdiciōrum (Lewis & Short); Cic. Brut. 59: ut hominis decus ingenium, sīc ingeniī ipsīus lūmen est ēloquentia (Lewis & Short)

    A favourite word of Cicero’s in his speeches (Lewis & Short); often of a person who is the pride of his order or his city.

Examples

  • est enim glōria solida quaedam rēs et expressa, nōn adumbrāta

    for glory is a solid thing, clear-cut, not a mere outlineCic. Tusc. 3.3 (Lewis & Short)

  • ut hominis decus ingenium, sīc ingeniī ipsīus lūmen est ēloquentia

    as a man’s glory is his mind, so the light of the mind itself is eloquenceCic. Brut. 59 (Lewis & Short)

See also honour, proud, thus passes the glory of the world, well done.
